articles.title: US Open tennis 2026 men’s semi-final: Alexander Zverev v Karen Khachanov – live
articles.summary: Updates from first men’s semi-final at 8pm BST, 3pm EST Andrew Lawrence: in praise of five-set tennis | Mail Billy. Karen Khachanov is in his first grand slam semi-final for three and a half years.
body: “There are people that you don’t see from the outside, but I think he’s somebody that works extremely hard,” were Zverev’s words about Khachanov during his press conference yesterday.

He’s on the practice courts more than most people. He’s always searching for solutions. He’s always trying to find new ways to get better. He has a great coach who I’ve known also since juniors. He’s been with him since juniors. That I respect a lot when people go together for a long time and go together a long way.
We call him ‘The Professor’ because he knows everything about tennis, and he knows every single string tension, knows what everybody does, so that’s quite fun.

Zverev leads the career head-to-head 6-3 against Khachanov. They faced each other twice during the North American swing last year, with Khachanov winning in the Canadian Open semis but retiring in the fourth round at Cincinnati. Their only grand slam meeting was at the 2018 French Open, when Zverev won in five sets in the fourth round.

articles.title: Solheim Cup: USA fightback sparks hope of away win after Europe’s fast start
articles.summary: Scores level at 4-4 after day one. Europe fail to make advantage pay in fourballs. The rain poured and the United States roared. Hope had cascaded through the European contingent at this ­Solheim Cup during Friday afternoon until the sort of fightback that endorsed the sense that, come Sunday…
body: After a morning session that closed all square at 2-2, Europe surged ahead in three fourball matches. This felt like validation for Anna Nordqvist, the home captain. She had opted not to deploy any of the four players who returned two foursomes points – Maja Stark, Linn Grant, Leona Maguire and Esther Henseleit – after lunch.

Heads turned, especially in respect of Maguire. She was controversially lightly raced as Europe lost in the 2024 Solheim Cup. Victory for Maguire and Henseleit over Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan meant the Irishwoman became statistically the most successful European Solheim Cup player of all time. Maguire had cause to wonder why she was left on the sidelines; especially as Céline Boutier and Nanna Koerstz Madsen, who visibly toiled in the foursomes, slumped to a second defeat out of two. Megan Khang and Alison Lee cantered to a 5&3 fourball success in the one straightforward clash of the afternoon.

articles.title: England need 130 after thrilling Razaullah hitting
articles.summary: England face a chase of 130 to win the third Test after Pakistan debutant Razaullah produces some thrilling resistance on day three at Edgbaston.
body: Pakistan had battled to 318-8, still two runs behind, with potentially more than two hours of play remaining when Razaullah, the tourists' number nine, launched a sensational assault.
The 21-year-old's audacious 81 from 63 balls frazzled England and propelled Pakistan to 449. His nine sixes tied Ben Stokes' record for the number of maximums in a Test innings in England.

Razaullah shared an eighth-wicket stand of 121 with Muhammad Abbas, who whacked two sixes of his own in his 42. Finally, Razaullah was stumped off Lawrence to end the day and signal the beginning of England's chase on Saturday.
Pakistan deserved to drag the match into a weekend, restoring a modicum of pride to what has been a shambolic tour.

articles.title: Leading athletes still waiting on large sums owed by ill-fated Grand Slam Track
articles.summary: GST founder Michael Johnson said he ‘got the athletes paid’ Money stuck in escrow account after bankruptcy filing. Grand Slam Track athletes have still only received 50% of their earnings nearly 15 months on from the collapse of Michael Johnson’s ill-fated venture.
body: Many of the Grand Slam stars are at the Ultimate Championships here in Budapest, where they will compete for a $10m prize fund, the richest in the sport’s history, with first prizes of $150,000 for individual events.
However four leading agents have told the Guardian that their athletes are still waiting on large sums of money from GST, despite Johnson claiming last month that he had “got the athletes paid”.

Johnson, a four-time Olympic champion and BBC pundit, launched GST in April last year, with the promise to revolutionise the sport with huge prizes and salaries. But it collapsed after only three events, before organisers voluntarily filed for bankruptcy in the US in December.

Athletes ended up receiving half their earnings last October, but have not had anything since. Their agents are hopeful that they will receive another sum in the region of 25% from an escrow account in the next month or two.

articles.title: Mas closes on first Vuelta after Dunbar reels in Buitrago to win stage 19 summit finish
articles.summary: Pinarello Q36.5 rider Dunbar wins stage by 14 seconds. Mas maintains his 1min 37sec cushion in red jersey race. Irishman Eddie Dunbar secured a stunning last-ditch victory on stage 19 of the Vuelta a España as Spaniard Enric Mas maintained his overall lead with only one mountain stage remaining…
body: The 30-year-old caught and passed Colombian Santiago Buitrago with just 300 metres left of the mountainous 210km slog from Vélez-Málaga to Peñas Blancas.

Bahrain Victorious rider Buitrago struck out for home inside the final 2km to distance his three breakaway companions, including Dunbar, who initially did not react. However, the Pinarello Q36.5 rider launched his counterattack in the final kilometre and wasted little time in reeling in Buitrago, who is the leader of the mountains classification. Dunbar finished 14sec ahead of Buitrago, with his British teammate, Thomas Gloag, coming home in third 23sec back.

“It’s incredible, I really didn’t expect this today,” said Dunbar. “I even said in the team radio after about 50 or 60km that today wasn’t my day. I wasn’t feeling good. Then I ended up in the break and my legs came around a bit.”
Movistar’s Mas comfortably held on to his 1min 37sec lead over four-time former champion Primoz Roglic as the overall contenders crossed the line together.

articles.title: Benn defies concerns to make weight for Garcia bout
articles.summary: Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia both comfortably make the welterweight limit for their WBC title fight despite concerns at how they would fare on the scales.
body: Briton Benn, 29, weighed in at 10st 6lb (66kg) for Saturday's bout - half a pound heavier than the champion.
The official weigh-in took place behind closed doors at the UFC Apex on Friday, in front of about 50 members of the media, before a ceremonial event later in the day which will be open to the public.

Garcia has won 25 of his 28 professional contests, including 20 knockout victories, with two defeats and one no-contest. Benn has 25 wins - 14 by knockout - and one loss, and is fighting for his first world title.
American Garcia, 28, won the WBC belt with a dominant points victory over Mario Barrios in February and is making his first defence against Benn.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Slams ‘Gutless’ ESPN Over Lack of Coverage of Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel Scandal
articles.summary: NFL star Aaron Rodgers did not mince words when he slammed ESPN over its lack of coverage of former journalist Dianna Russini ‘s alleged affair with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel.
body: “I also said you’re a gutless organization because they haven’t said anything,” Rodgers, 42, said during his Thursday, September 10, appearance on the Not Just Football with Cam Heyward show. “They spend so much time on certain issues but you won’t talk one second on the Dianna Russini situation.”

The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback went on to explain that ESPN reported on San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York ‘s prostitution scandal on the front page of its website, but failed to acknowledge the scandal involving Russini, 43, and Vrabel, 51.

“They will rotate the eight stories or whatever they have but they usually have like the one story that’s featured,” Rodgers continued. “That was the featured story. So you bring in how many millions of eyes to that situation. Why do you want to throw Jed York under the bus? I don’t know. But does that have the same effect as a reporter who’s, you know, has intimate relations with a coach, who has a vote for MVP, has a vote for coach of the year. I don’t know if she’s on the Hall of Fame [voting committee] or not but there’s voting stuff.”

articles.title: Alonso cannot leave F1 while uncompetitive - FIA boss
articles.summary: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem says it would be "not acceptable" for Fernando Alonso to leave F1 while he is in an uncompetitive position.
body: The 45-year-old two-time world champion is out of contract with Aston Martin at the end of this season and on Thursday said his decision on whether to stay in F1 would be made "not soon".
Aston Martin are 10th in the championship so far this season after producing an uncompetitive car, while engine partner Honda's power-unit is the least powerful on the grid.

Ben Sulayem, the head of motorsport's governing body, said at an event in Madrid on Friday: "There is no way we can allow Fernando to leave - Alonso, a great champion - to leave just because of the circumstances.
"That's not the way to leave the stage. He has to be successful and then he leaves whenever he wants, not because he was forced to leave because of the performance."

articles.title: Prosecutors seek up to 10 years prison over violent burglary of Donnarumma
articles.summary: French prosecutors on Friday sought prison terms of up to 10 years against three men accused of holding Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend captive during a violent burglary at their home in Paris.
body: The 27-year-old Donnarumma and Alessia Elefante were bound and threatened during the terrifying ordeal in their luxury apartment on Avenue Montaigne in central Paris in July 2023, a court in the French capital heard.
At the time of the burglary, the Italian international played for Paris Saint-Germain, but he moved to Manchester City in 2025.
Prosecutors at the Paris Criminal Court requested prison sentences ranging from four to 10 years against the three men alleged to have orchestrated or participated in the violent burglary.

The harshest sentence of 10 years was sought for Ilyas Kherbouch, 21, alias "Ganito" -- who gained notoriety following his brazen escape from Villepinte prison in Seine-Saint-Denis, north of Paris last March.

articles.title: Remarkable Razaullah knock denies England series sweep inside three days
articles.summary: England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday.
body: Pakistan enjoyed easily their finest day of what's otherwise been a dismal series but were still trailing by two when their eighth wicket fell early into the evening session, only for Razaullah to smash 81 off just 63 deliveries, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant.

He shared in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42), who himself hit two sixes before picking out point off Josh Tongue in the closing overs, while Razaullah's fun was finally ended - and the day's play - as he was stumped off Dan Lawrence (2-17).

England, guilty of losing the plot in the final session, will now look to chase down 130 on day four, a far stiffer target than initially looked likely, albeit one they should still reel in to clinch a first ever home series whitewash of Pakistan.
The tourists might be cursing not testing England further, with Shan Masood (95) and Babar Azam (76) both spurning golden opportunities to score the first century of the series.

articles.title: Sunderland v Arsenal: Key stats and talking points
articles.summary: Arsenal will look to extend their perfect start to the new season when they face Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Saturday (20:00 BST) in the Premier League. The Gunners head to Wearside on the back of an impressive win over Napoli in the Champions League on Wednesday.
body: Sunderland have bounced back well after an opening-weekend loss to Ipswich Town, taking four points from games against Fulham at home and Brentford away in their subsequent fixtures.

In the early weeks of last season, Sunderland were one of the few sides to give the Gunners problems. Dan Ballard 's opening goal against Arsenal in November 2025 was the first time Mikel Arteta's side had conceded in eight games at the time; a stoppage-time strike from Brian Brobbey earned the Black Cats a 2-2 draw.
While they are capable of giving Arsenal a bloody nose, getting over the line and beating the Gunners has not been easy for Sunderland down the years.

Sunderland have only won one of their last 14 league games against Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. The Black Cats actually only have one victory in 29 Premier League meetings against the Gunners, and are winless in 17.

articles.title: Antonelli sets pace as Lindblad suffers first F1 crash at challenging Madring
articles.summary: World championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest on Formula 1's first day of running at the Spanish Grand Prix's new Madrid circuit as the hugely challenging nature of the Madring was exhibited by a big crash for British rookie Arvid Lindblad.
body: After being outpaced by his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the day's first session, Antonelli produced a quicker time of 1:33.662 in Practice Two to edge out Ferrari duo Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton by little more than a tenth of a second.

The timesheet was further evidence of Antonelli's sky-high confidence, which was elevated by a stunning victory at the Italian Grand Prix last weekend as he won his home race from 19th on the grid to move 66 points clear of Russell at the top of the standings with 10 rounds of the 2026 season remaining.

On the evidence of Friday's sessions, Mercedes and Ferrari are closely matched and could deliver an exciting pole contest in qualifying on Saturday, with huge excitement in the Spanish capital as F1 returns to the city for the first time since 1981.
Many had predicted a high number of red flags on Friday - and throughout the rest of the weekend - due to the tight and punishing nature of a circuit that the field have never raced at before.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Backing Pierre Bonnard to bag 10th Leger for O'Brien
articles.summary: Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle marks your card for the 250th St Leger and a stellar undercard at Doncaster on Saturday - live on Sky Sports Racing – and has a look at Leopardstown.
body: Who stands in the way of Aidan O'Brien and a brilliant 10th success in the world's oldest Classic, the Betfred St Leger Stakes (3.35) at Doncaster on Saturday? He saddles four runners on the 250th anniversary of the great race including probable favourite Christmas Day, who is bidding to become the first Derby winner to triumph since Reference Point 39 years ago.

Aidan's son Joseph O'Brien looks the most likely opponent to spoil the Ballydoyle party with the impressive Enceladus, who steps up to Group One company for the first time after excelling in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Group Three Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

However, I believe Aidan can complete the feat - not with Christmas Day but with his tough stable companion PIERRE BONNARD, who finished in front of him in the Great Voltigeur Stakes at York last month. This more demanding test of stamina is what he's been crying out for, and he can write his own piece of history.
